title: Repairing a Bridge Without Closing It
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript:
A bridge inspection rarely begins with a dramatic discovery. More often, engineers compare a series of small measurements and ask whether the structure is changing faster than expected. A crack that appears alarming in a photograph may have remained stable for years, while a less visible movement around a joint can signal a developing problem.

During a recent maintenance project, a regional engineering team installed sensors on an older road bridge. The devices measured how the deck moved as vehicles crossed. To interpret these readings, the engineers also recorded temperature, because metal expands on a warm afternoon even when no damage is present. Measurements taken at different temperatures could not be compared without allowing for this ordinary response.

The data showed an unusual pattern near one support. Movement increased when heavy vehicles travelled in a particular lane, but returned to its previous level after they passed. A closer inspection found that a bearing, which should have allowed controlled movement, was partly blocked by accumulated debris. Clearing the bearing restored much of its function without requiring a major structural replacement.

The bridge remained open during most of the work. However, the team temporarily restricted the affected lane while the bearing was cleaned. They rejected a proposal to remove the sensors immediately afterwards. Continued monitoring was needed to establish whether the improvement persisted through colder weather, when the structure would behave differently.

For engineering students, the case demonstrates the value of interpreting measurements in context. A sensor does not label a bridge safe or unsafe. It records a response that must be connected to traffic, weather and physical inspection. The most useful outcome was not simply a large collection of data, but a specific explanation that led to a proportionate repair.

questions.prompt: Why did the engineers record temperature as well as bridge movement?
options: Temperature determined the number of vehicles allowed on the road.
Warm weather prevented the sensors from recording any data.
Normal expansion could otherwise be mistaken for a structural change.
The bridge had to be painted at a fixed temperature.
questions.answer: Normal expansion could otherwise be mistaken for a structural change.
questions.explanation: 金属随温度正常膨胀，需排除这一因素才能解释结构变化。

questions.prompt: What caused the unusual movement near one support?
options: Debris had partly blocked a bearing.
A new lane had been built in the wrong place.
All the sensors had been installed backwards.
The bridge deck had recently been replaced.
questions.answer: Debris had partly blocked a bearing.
questions.explanation: 检查发现应允许受控移动的支座被堆积物部分堵塞。

questions.prompt: Why were the sensors kept in place after the repair?
options: They were required to count the cleaning staff.
The team wanted to check whether the improvement lasted in colder weather.
Removing them would have required replacing the whole deck.
The team had decided to close the bridge permanently.
questions.answer: The team wanted to check whether the improvement lasted in colder weather.
questions.explanation: 工程师需要继续观察改进是否能在寒冷季节保持。

questions.prompt: What lesson does the speaker draw from the project?
options: More data always make physical inspections unnecessary.
Photographs provide a complete measure of structural safety.
Every unusual movement requires replacement of the bridge.
Measurements become useful when linked to conditions and physical evidence.
questions.answer: Measurements become useful when linked to conditions and physical evidence.
questions.explanation: 结尾强调数据要结合交通、天气和现场检查才能导向恰当维修。
